checks.finding: Every in-scope requirement (REQ-001..REQ-009) resolves to one or more independently identified acceptance criteria with concrete, measurable pass/fail conditions (e.g. AC-001..AC-011 for REQ-001's glob/normalization/schema-conformance clauses, AC-026..AC-036+AC-052..AC-055 for REQ-004's three derived-state/Fail-1..6/reachability behaviors, AC-037..AC-041 for REQ-005's digest scope). acceptance-tests.md maps each AC 1:1 to a TEST ID with a concrete fixture/assertion description. No requirement in the Goals section lacks a measurable observable outcome.

All nine stated Goals (REQ-001 through REQ-009) have matching acceptance criteria: REQ-001->AC-001..011, REQ-002->AC-012..018, REQ-003->AC-019..025, REQ-004->AC-026..036 and AC-052..055, REQ-005->AC-037..041, REQ-006->AC-042..044, REQ-007->AC-045..047, REQ-008->AC-048..049, REQ-009->AC-050..051. acceptance-tests.md's table confirms every AC-001..AC-055 maps to a TEST-ID and cites its parent REQ.

Acceptance criteria describe concrete, externally observable artifacts: specific glob-match outcomes on named fixture paths (AC-001, AC-002, AC-007), exact exit codes and evidence-record state string values (AC-027, AC-028, AC-052, AC-053), byte-for-byte stdout JSON diffing between wrapper runtimes (AC-050), and file-existence/hash checks (AC-036, AC-054, AC-055). None rely on vague intent language without a concrete observable.

Non-goals section explicitly excludes: project-context.yaml schema definition, Facet Manifest schema definition, Epic A1 canonicalizer reimplementation, Capability Registry/Registry gate projection, Provider Bindings file schema definition, and any change to sdd-hook-guard's own enforcement logic. Dependencies section further scopes exactly which cross-epic artifacts are hard vs. non-blocking dependencies.

Material constraints are explicit: a dedicated Security Boundaries section covers protected-file tamper-evidence scope (two-tier defense per ADR-0019), credential-block exclusion for Provider Bindings, and submodule/symlink reference-only boundaries. A Roles and Permissions section fixes the human-only approval boundary for protected-file human-copy application and task Approval state. Compatibility/migration is covered by the fail-closed schema-conformance and cross-epic-template fixtures rather than left implicit.

The Risks section lists five concrete high-risk claims and each is paired with an explicit validation surface: a dedicated fixture/AC (e.g. AC-032 for the exclude-as-include invariant, AC-038/AC-040 for digest-vs-staleness selectivity, AC-011/AC-042/044's fail-closed discipline for the cross-epic coupling). No high-risk claim is left without a named acceptance criterion or fixture path.
